description: Conformance cases for the skill publishing rules. Each case is one skill folder, skills/<name>/, and gives its expect result in this check: pass means no errors (warnings are allowed), fail means at least one error, and error is a fragment of this repository's own message. Another tool that validates or publishes these skills should give the same result on the cases for the rules it implements; some rules here are stricter than any other tool's. A case with base compares the skill with that merge-base copy, and base: null means the pull request adds the skill. files: null with a base means the pull request removes the folder. retired: true means the path belonged to a skill removed earlier. content_hash pins the content hash function with a golden fixture. A file is given as UTF-8 text or as base64 bytes, with an optional Git mode (default 100644). Published files in cases are .md, except in the extension and path cases, which use extensions that skills/.gitignore must never allow or names with no extension, so results don't depend on the allowlist; where a case must show that a file is published, the file starts with #!. Cases for the size limits are in the unit tests, because they need large files. validate_skills.py runs every case before it checks any skill.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 over the sorted records <path>\u0000<sha256 hex of the file bytes>\n, one per published file, with paths sorted by their UTF-8 bytes, so references/a-b.md comes before references/a/b.md, unlike in a folder walk. Every implementation must compute sha256 for these files.
